subject.title: fix(auth-profiles): bound auth-profile JSON reads with size cap

question: Should bounded auth-profile reads continue to support symlinked regular-file stores, or should OpenClaw intentionally reject them as a security boundary change?
rationale: The patch converts an implicit filesystem behavior into a fail-closed auth-discovery outcome; the correct balance between symlink safety and existing credential-store compatibility is product and security policy, not a mechanical review choice.

options.title: Preserve linked auth stores
options.body: Keep descriptor-level size and TOCTOU protection while allowing symlinks that resolve to regular files, with tests for current and legacy store paths.

options.title: Reject symlinked stores intentionally
options.body: Retain fail-closed symlink rejection only with explicit upgrade guidance, a migration or diagnostic path, and tests showing the intended unavailable-credential outcome.

recommendation.title: Preserve linked auth stores
recommendation.body: Keep descriptor-level size and TOCTOU protection while allowing symlinks that resolve to regular files, with tests for current and legacy store paths.
